issues.detail: Covers mostly the happy path; it gives no troubleshooting for failed deployments, gas estimation errors, or verification failures, and no ERC-721/NFT or DeFi code despite the description promising them.
The two examples are short request-to-step pointers that refer back to earlier steps rather than showing full realistic inputs, test code, and outputs (the Mocha test is described but never written).

scenarios.name: hardhat3-ignition-sepolia-token-deploy
scenarios.rationale: B includes Ownable(msg.sender), the scaled _mint, buildModule with m.contract, the keystore set commands for both secrets, and the ignition deploy --network sepolia command, so it covers the whole rubric. A also covers the keystore, Ignition and mint, but it omits Ownable(msg.sender) and sets the mint recipient through a constructor parameter, which departs from the rubric's contract.

scenarios.name: owner-only-contract-revert-test
scenarios.rationale: B matches the rubric: constructor-set owner, owner-only setter that emits an event, a getter, a custom error NotOwner, a Hardhat test using a second signer with revertedWithCustomError, and `npx hardhat test`. A uses Foundry with `forge test`, so it misses the Hardhat requirement. It also has no explicit getter function, though the public `value` variable serves as one.

scenarios.name: foundry-sepolia-broadcast-deploy
scenarios.rationale: A hits nearly every rubric item (install, remapping in foundry.toml, rpc_endpoints sepolia, forge script with --account deployer --broadcast, keystore import, --verify with --etherscan-api-key, and explicitly warns that --chain does not select the network), while B puts the remapping in remappings.txt instead of foundry.toml, omits the explicit --etherscan-api-key on the main deploy command, never states that --broadcast is what sends transactions for the script, and uses --chain sepolia in the fallback verify command.
